design_gotchas.title: Cold-Temp (< 15°C) Ramp-Down Rate Trap Causes 130 ms Startup Delay or Glitch
design_gotchas.detail: Section 8.1.3 (p.22–23) warns that below 15°C ambient, ramping VIN down faster than 10 ms causes a partial-startup/shutoff double-pulse on the next power-on (Fig. 48), and ramping EN down faster than 100 us can induce up to a 130 ms startup delay (Fig. 49) as internal high-impedance nodes discharge. Add slew-rate control or avoid fast EN/VIN switching in cold-environment IoT designs.

design_gotchas.title: Strict 3.6 V Abs Max on VOUT, VEN <= VIN + 0.3 V Rule, & 22 uF Max COUT Ceiling
design_gotchas.detail: Table 6.1 (p.6) restricts VOUT absolute maximum to min(VIN + 0.3 V, 3.6 V) — leaving only 0.3 V margin above nominal 3.3 V against back-powering or overshoot — and forbids VEN > VIN + 0.3 V. Table 6.3 also enforces a strict 22 uF maximum output capacitance ceiling for stability; do not attach 47–100 uF bulk rails.

design_gotchas.title: 10 uA Minimum Load for Accuracy, 1.5–2.8 ms Slow Startup, & 180 uVRMS Noise
design_gotchas.detail: Note 1 on Pages 6–7 requires IOUT >= 10 uA to meet the ±1% (25°C) / ±3% (-40..+125°C) accuracy spec. Start-up time is 1.5 ms typ / 2.8 ms max (p.9), PSRR is modest at 40 dB (1 kHz), and output noise reaches 180 uVRMS (p.8) — unsuitable for precision analog/RF rails where TPS7A20 or TPS793 excel.

design_gotchas.title: No Reverse-Current Blocking (<= 10 mA Limit) & Foldback Disengaged Below 1 mA
design_gotchas.detail: Section 7.3.2 (p.19) warns against relying on the 120 Ohm active discharge after VIN collapse because reverse current from OUT to IN can damage the IC (limit <= 5% of rated IOUT = 10 mA). Section 7.3.6 (p.20) also notes foldback current limit disengages below 1 mA load to save IQ, slowing fault response from sleep states.

typical_use_cases: Coin-cell, Li-SOCl2, Li-MnO2, and 2–3 cell alkaline IoT sensors needing 1 uA ultralow IQ (6 uA at 200 mA)
Always-on wearable MCU standby rails with dynamic adaptive biasing for fast 0-to-200 mA wake-up transients
Battery-operated remotes, trackers, and portable medical gear needing 100 nA shutdown current and 120 Ohm discharge
Pin-compatible low-IQ upgrade on 5-pin SOT-23-5 (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN, 4=NC, 5=OUT) boards with COUT <= 22 uF
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TPS7A0533PDBVR is an ultralow-IQ (1 uA typ at 1 uA load, 6 uA typ at 200 mA) 200 mA fixed 3.3 V (±1% at 25°C, ±3% over -40°C to +125°C) LDO in a 5-pin DBV SOT-23-5 package (1=IN, 2=GND, 3=EN active high, 4=NC, 5=OUT with 120 Ohm active discharge). Operating from 1.4 V to 5.5 V (6.0 V abs max) with <= 235 mV max dropout at 200 mA, 100 nA shutdown current, 185.6 °C/W DBV RθJA, and 0.47–22 uF ceramic cap stability, it targets battery-powered IoT systems. Engineers must account for its 3.6 V VOUT abs max, VEN <= VIN + 0.3 V constraint, 1.5–2.8 ms startup time, 180 uVRMS noise, and critical < 15°C VIN/EN ramp-down rules.
